decisive_items: Epidermal acanthosis, spongiosis, and acantholytic keratinocytes.
Foci of eosinophilic spongiosis in the epidermis.
abundant intercellular deposition of IgG and C3 in the upper two-thirds of the epidermis
response.rationale: The histopathologic findings of acantholysis and eosinophilic spongiosis plus intercellular epidermal IgG/C3 deposition are diagnostic of pemphigus. The ANA positivity and photodistribution are nonspecific, and the negative anti-Ro/La and anti-Smith antibodies with normal complement argue against lupus erythematosus. Dermatomyositis lacks the characteristic histopathologic and immunofluorescence findings.

rejected.why: ANA positivity, photosensitivity, and basement-membrane IgG/C3 are suggestive, but negative anti-Ro/La and anti-Smith, normal complement, and the presence of acantholysis and intercellular epidermal IgG/C3 are not typical for lupus erythematosus.

Photosensitive pruritic plaques could suggest dermatomyositis, but there is no supporting muscle or histopathologic evidence, and the acantholysis and intercellular IgG/C3 pattern point away from this diagnosis.
